title: Companion App Privacy Confession Booth
oneLiner: A playful but pointed privacy mirror that helps AI companion users reveal what intimate data, token fees, and emotional hooks they are trading away.
previewUrl: pending Stitch export in Phase B
targetUser: Curious or lonely AI companion users who want connection but feel uneasy about privacy, pricing, and emotional dependency.
keyUx: Answer confession-card prompts about what you would tell a bot, what you would pay for, and what would hurt to lose; the app returns a privacy risk mirror and safer-use pact.
spread_trigger: Users share a redacted privacy mirror because it is funny, embarrassing, and a little too accurate.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "Companion App Privacy Confession Booth" for Curious or lonely AI companion users who want connection but feel uneasy about privacy, pricing, and emotional dependency.. The app is based on observed user pull from S16: Viral AI prank/photo apps market fake relationship edits and shock transformations as shareable attention products. S17: Users interested in companion bots worry they are feeding intimate psychological profiles to advertisers. The app should use a Confession Booth around the trigger moment "Answer confession-card prompts about what you would tell a bot, what you would pay for, and what would hurt to lose; the app returns a privacy risk mirror and safer-use pact." and make the first screen communicate "A playful but pointed privacy mirror that helps AI companion users reveal what intimate data, token fees, and emotional hooks they are trading away.". Build the core workflow around user-entered evidence and produce redacted companion-risk mirror and safer-use pact. Required sections: Confession card stack; Intimacy data map; Token and paywall creep meter; Ad-targeting fear checklist; Boundary pact builder; Delete/export reminder; Shareable redacted mirror. Emotional pressure to make visible: 외로움 / 성욕. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with playful-experimental mood with neon confession cards, privacy-warning contrast, and humorous but humane microcopy. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like Confession Booth.

sourceSignals.source: Apple App Store listing for VIRL AI video/photo prank edit app

sourceSignals.action: Users create reaction-bait edits that invite friends to judge whether the moment is real, funny, or too invasive.
